newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG sells Metallbank to Schmidtbank.
newsitem.headline: MG sells Metallbank to Schmidtbank.

text.p: German metals and trading group Metallgesellschaft AG said on Wednesday it was selling its banking operations, Metallbank GmbH, to Schmidtbank KGaA.

MG, which is still recovering from huge losses chalked up on U.S. oil deals in late 1993, said in a statement that the move was an early response to consolidation trends in the banking industry and would help strengthen its balance sheet.

Deutsche Boerse announced soon after the announcement was made that MG's shares would be suspended in afternoon trading, and resume trade on the IBIS computer system at 1515 GMT. MG was up eight pfennigs at 27.58 marks.
"With this sale, Metallgesellschaft is responding early to the strong process of concentration in the banking sector and is creating new growth and profit opportunities for itself," MG said.

The new owner of Metallbank, SchmidtBank, is a private banking group with 130 branches in Bavaria, Saxony and Thuringia. MG said the deal offered SchmidtBank access to the German market. The deal is back-dated to October 1, 1996.
MG management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen said the sale would help to increase shareholder value. "The separation from Metallbank has helped us to optimise the group for shareholders," he said.
Neukirchen, brought in to turn MG around after it slipped close to bankruptcy in 1993, has led the company into heavy divestments, in a bid to concentrate attention on core activities.
